column3: *** "LERENA de L[erena], JOSEFA, m, 43, VIUDA, R. Oriental" *** - born about 1852. On the lines above, the same enumerator writes married women as [maiden surname] + "de L.", so if he is consistent she was BORN A LERENA AND MARRIED A LERENA

column1: Death at Montevideo
column3: *** "JOSEFA LORENA LERENA TRAIBEL", aged 96, born 1851. Parents: AVELINO LERENA and AMBROCIA TRAIBEL *** - which places the LERENA TRAIBEL branch this archive has named since its first week

column1: # *** WHAT FITS. *** The 1895 census gives her age as 43, implying birth about 1852; the death record
# says 1851. One year apart, which is nothing. Both are "R. Oriental" / Montevideo women. A woman who
# was in her brother-in-law's Buenos Aires house in 1895 and died at Montevideo in 1947 is entirely
# ordinary - the family crossed that river constantly.
# *** WHAT DOES NOT FIT, OR IS NOT TESTED. ***
# - The 1947 death record names NO SPOUSE. The census woman is a VIUDA. Neither contradicts the
#   other, but neither confirms it either.
# - The census form "Lerena de Lerena" would mean she married a man of her own surname. The death
#   record gives her as LERENA TRAIBEL - her parents' surnames, which is what a Uruguayan death record
#   gives whether or not she married.
# - *** NOTHING LINKS AVELINO LERENA TO SANCHO. *** An Avelino Lerena stood godfather at the Catedral
#   in 1833 to a child of Justa Pastora Lerena, Sancho's daughter - which is suggestive and no more.
#   Avelino's own parents are named in no record found here.
# *** SO: ONE STRONG CANDIDATE IDENTIFICATION, RECORDED AS THREE ROWS AND NOT MERGED. ***
# What would settle it: Josefa's MARRIAGE record. If she married a Lerena, the census reading is
# right and this family contains a LERENA-LERENA MARRIAGE one generation before Juan Carlos and
# Maria - which is the pattern the whole search turns on.
